extracted.intended_audience: Authors, referees, associate editors, and editors submitting to or handling manuscripts for the Annals of Statistics (Institute of Mathematical Statistics).
extracted.subtask_description: Ethical principles and responsibilities for authors, referees, associate editors, and editors handling submissions to the Annals of Statistics, covering plagiarism, authorship communication, citation, confidentiality, conflicts of interest, and review conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism, including self-transcription
rubrics_metrics.description: All submitted material must be the authors’ own work, original to the submission, unless specifically stated as having another origin, which must be clearly identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Original to the submission’ covers not only previously published work but also unpublished work the authors have submitted or plan to submit elsewhere. This applies to original research and to literature review text or summaries of known aspects; paragraphs addressing such matters should not be copied from published or to-be-published work. Consider copyright issues. The Annals generally is not interested in publishing technical material closely related to results presented elsewhere (including conference proceedings) by the authors; this policy may differ from other fields but is common among major statistical journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corresponding author responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author must be an author familiar with the correct procedures for obtaining permissions and for submitting a paper, and share responsibility for ensuring that ethical principles are adhered to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the corresponding author is relatively inexperienced, more experienced colleagues (co-authors or others) must ensure the corresponding author is made fully aware of their responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keeping co-authors informed
rubrics_metrics.description: All authors must be fully informed, by the corresponding author, of the paper's submission and related correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All authors must receive copies of relevant correspondence; the corresponding author must be willing and able to provide evidence to an Editor that all authors agreed to the submission and are fully aware of the submission's contents. Authors must also be kept timely informed of any editorial decisions concerning the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must cite all closely relevant literature, including unpublished or recently published work (including conference proceedings) of their own related to the submitted paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This citation requirement applies even when the related work is available only in preprint form; failure to cite closely related work may lead quickly to rejection. Items not readily available on the web should be uploaded as supplementary files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding editorial decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should understand the journal receives many more submissions than it can publish, so many worthy submissions are rejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions may be based in part on subjective criteria (e.g., timeliness, perceived level of general interest). Authors may not always agree with decisions but should remain professional and cordial in communications with editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of a paper under review
rubrics_metrics.description: Both the content of a submitted paper and the fact that it is under review are confidential and should not be disclosed to individuals not part of the review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referees who wish to review together with a student or collaborator should seek the permission of the associate editor beforehand. Referees, Associate Editors and Editors must not take advantage of information obtained via their role. After review, referees should destroy the manuscript and any supplementary material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunities in review
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees, Associate Editors and Editors should avoid any bias in the review of manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid bias due to gender, age, racial or ethnic origin, affiliation, or reputation of authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Referees, Associate Editors and Editors are expected to be constructive and polite when writing reports; comments must be based solely on the work under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defamatory or personal comments must be avoided. Reviewers will be asked to remove unprofessional remarks from their reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of reviewers' identities
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors, Associate Editors and referees must take all reasonable lengths to ensure confidentiality of the process; identities of referees should not be revealed to authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Associate Editors and referees must not knowingly identify their involvement in the review to authors, even after the process is completed. If a reviewer's identity is inadvertently revealed to an author, an Editor must be notified immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of referees
rubrics_metrics.description: An Associate Editor must take all reasonable precautions to ensure referees do not have conflicts of interest (e.g., personal/professional association or competing work).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sole basis for choice of referees should be the scientific case: their knowledge of the field, absence of conflict of interest, and willingness and capacity to provide useful, relevant and timely reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflicts of interest for Associate Editors and Editors
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and Associate Editors must not handle papers where one or more authors are departmental colleagues, current close collaborators, or close personal associates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should also be aware of potential conflicts when handling papers that compete directly with their own current work; in case of doubt the manuscript should be reassigned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors reviewing for other journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors should refrain from reviewing for other statistical journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures Editors have sufficient time and energy for IMS editorial work and helps keep Editors' decisions independent of whether the paper was previously submitted elsewhere.
